passages.text: Now in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was set before him, I took the wine and gave it to the king. I had never been sad in his presence, so the king said to me, “Why is your face sad, though you are not ill? This could only be sadness of the heart.” I was overwhelmed with fear and replied to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should I not be sad when the city where my fathers are buried lies in ruins, and its gates have been destroyed by fire?”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah served as the cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia.
It was the month of Nisan.
This was the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes’ reign.
Wine was set before the king.
I took the wine.
I gave the wine to the king.
I had never been sad in the king’s presence before.
The king noticed my sadness.
The king asked me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick?”
The king said, “This must be sadness of the heart.”
I became very afraid.
I answered the king.
I said, “May the king live forever!”
I said, “Why should I not be sad?”
I said, “The city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins.”
I said, “Its gates have been destroyed by fire.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ נִיסָ֗ן שְׁנַ֥ת עֶשְׂרִ֛ים לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥סְתְּא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ יַ֣יִן לְפָנָ֑יו וָאֶשָּׂ֤א אֶת־ הַיַּ֙יִן֙ וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלֹא־ הָיִ֥יתִי רַ֖ע לְפָנָֽיו׃ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מַדּ֣וּעַ׀ פָּנֶ֣יךָ רָעִ֗ים וְאַתָּה֙ אֵֽינְךָ֣ חוֹלֶ֔ה אֵ֣ין זֶ֔ה כִּי־ אִ֖ם רֹ֣עַֽ לֵ֑ב וָאִירָ֖א הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃ וָאֹמַ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לְעוֹלָ֣ם יִחְיֶ֑ה מַדּ֜וּעַ לֹא־ יֵרְע֣וּ פָנַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָעִ֜יר בֵּית־ קִבְר֤וֹת אֲבֹתַי֙ חֲרֵבָ֔ה וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ אֻכְּל֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃ס

passages.text: “What is your request?” replied the king. So I prayed to the God of heaven and answered the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you send me to Judah, to the city where my fathers are buried, so that I may rebuild it.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to me.
He asked, “What do you request?”
I am Nehemiah.
I served as cupbearer to King Artaxerxes.
I prayed to the God of heaven.
I answered the king.
I said, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, send me to Judah.”
Judah is the land of my ancestors.
The city where my fathers are buried is in Judah.
I ask to go there so I may rebuild the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לִי֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַל־ מַה־ זֶּ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ וָֽאֶתְפַּלֵּ֔ל אֶל־ אֱלֹהֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ וָאֹמַ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב וְאִם־ יִיטַ֥ב עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר תִּשְׁלָחֵ֣נִי אֶל־ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־ עִ֛יר קִבְר֥וֹת אֲבֹתַ֖י וְאֶבְנֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Then the king, with the queen seated beside him, asked me, “How long will your journey take, and when will you return?” So it pleased the king to send me, and I set a time.
passages.sermon:
King Artaxerxes sat on his throne.
The queen sat beside him.
The king spoke to me.
He asked, “How long will your journey take?”
He also asked, “When will you return?”
The king was pleased to send me.
I set a time for my return.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ לִ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וְהַשֵּׁגַ֣ל׀ יוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת אֶצְל֗וֹ עַד־ מָתַ֛י יִהְיֶ֥ה מַֽהֲלָכֲךָ֖ וּמָתַ֣י תָּשׁ֑וּב וַיִּיטַ֤ב לִפְנֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֔נִי וָֽאֶתְּנָ֥ה ל֖וֹ זְמָֽן׃

passages.text: I also said to him, “If it pleases the king, may letters be given to me for the governors west of the Euphrates, so that they will grant me safe passage until I reach Judah.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah spoke to the king.
Nehemiah was a servant of the king.
Nehemiah wanted to return to Judah.
Nehemiah said, "If it pleases the king, give me letters."
The letters should be for the governors west of the Euphrates River.
The governors control the land between Persia and Judah.
The letters will tell the governors to let Nehemiah pass safely.
The letters will allow Nehemiah to travel until he reaches Judah.
passages.original: וָאוֹמַר֮ לַמֶּלֶךְ֒ אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב אִגְּרוֹת֙ יִתְּנוּ־ לִ֔י עַֽל־ פַּחֲו֖וֹת עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר אֲשֶׁר֙ יַעֲבִיר֔וּנִי עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־ אָב֖וֹא אֶל־ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And may I have a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king’s forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel to the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will occupy.” And because the gracious hand of my God was upon me, the king granted my requests.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah spoke to the king of Persia.
Nehemiah asked for a letter to Asaph.
Asaph was the keeper of the king’s forest.
Nehemiah wanted timber from Asaph.
Nehemiah needed timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple.
Nehemiah needed timber for the city wall.
Nehemiah needed timber for the house he would occupy.
The king gave Nehemiah what he requested.
God’s gracious hand was upon Nehemiah.
passages.original: וְאִגֶּ֡רֶת אֶל־ אָסָף֩ שֹׁמֵ֨ר הַפַּרְדֵּ֜ס אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתֶּן־ לִ֣י עֵצִ֡ים לְ֠קָרוֹת אֶת־ שַׁעֲרֵ֨י הַבִּירָ֤ה אֲשֶׁר־ לַבַּ֙יִת֙ וּלְחוֹמַ֣ת הָעִ֔יר וְלַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁר־ אָב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיִּתֶּן־ לִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּיַד־ אֱלֹהַ֖י הַטּוֹבָ֥ה עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: Then I went to the governors west of the Euphrates and gave them the king’s letters. The king had also sent army officers and cavalry with me.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a Jewish leader.
He traveled to the governors west of the Euphrates River.
He gave the governors the letters from the king.
The king sent army officers with Nehemiah.
The king also sent cavalry with him.
passages.original: וָֽאָב֗וֹא אֶֽל־ פַּֽחֲווֹת֙ עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֔ר וָאֶתְּנָ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אִגְּר֣וֹת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח עִמִּי֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׂ֥רֵי חַ֖יִל וּפָרָשִֽׁים׃פ

passages.text: But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about this, they were deeply disturbed that someone had come to seek the well-being of the Israelites.
passages.sermon:
Sanballat was a Horonite.
Tobiah was an Ammonite official.
Sanballat and Tobiah heard about this.
They learned that someone had come to help the Israelites.
This news upset them very much.
They felt deeply disturbed.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע סַנְבַלַּ֣ט הַחֹרֹנִ֗י וְטֽוֹבִיָּה֙ הָעֶ֣בֶד הָֽעַמֹּנִ֔י וַיֵּ֥רַע לָהֶ֖ם רָעָ֣ה גְדֹלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א אָדָ֔ם לְבַקֵּ֥שׁ טוֹבָ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: After I had arrived in Jerusalem and had been there three days, I set out at night with a few men. I did not tell anyone what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal with me was the one on which I was riding.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a Jewish leader.
He arrived in Jerusalem.
He stayed there for three days.
After three days, Nehemiah got up at night.
A few men went with him.
Nehemiah did not tell anyone his plans.
God had put something on Nehemiah’s heart to do for Jerusalem.
Nehemiah kept this purpose secret.
Nehemiah had only one animal with him.
He rode on this animal.
No other animals were with him.
passages.original: וָאָב֖וֹא אֶל־ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וָאֱהִי־ שָׁ֖ם יָמִ֥ים שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃ וָאָק֣וּם׀ לַ֗יְלָה אֲנִי֮ וַאֲנָשִׁ֣ים׀ מְעַט֮ עִמִּי֒ וְלֹא־ הִגַּ֣דְתִּי לְאָדָ֔ם מָ֗ה אֱלֹהַי֙ נֹתֵ֣ן אֶל־ לִבִּ֔י לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת לִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּבְהֵמָה֙ אֵ֣ין עִמִּ֔י כִּ֚י אִם־ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י רֹכֵ֥ב בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: So I went out at night through the Valley Gate toward the Well of the Serpent and the Dung Gate, and I inspected the walls of Jerusalem that had been broken down and the gates that had been destroyed by fire.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was in Jerusalem.
He went out at night.
He left through the Valley Gate.
He went toward the Well of the Serpent.
He went toward the Dung Gate.
He inspected the walls of Jerusalem.
The walls had been broken down.
He saw the gates of Jerusalem.
The gates had been destroyed by fire.
passages.original: וָאֵצְאָ֨ה בְשַֽׁעַר־ הַגַּ֜יא לַ֗יְלָה וְאֶל־ פְּנֵי֙ עֵ֣ין הַתַּנִּ֔ין וְאֶל־ שַׁ֖עַר הָאַשְׁפֹּ֑ת וָאֱהִ֨י שֹׂבֵ֜ר בְּחוֹמֹ֤ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ אֲשֶׁר־ הַמְפֹרוָצִים וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ אֻכְּל֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to get through; so I went up the valley by night and inspected the wall. Then I headed back and reentered through the Valley Gate.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was in Jerusalem at night.
He went to the Fountain Gate.
He went to the King’s Pool.
There was no room for the animal under him to pass through.
Nehemiah went up the valley at night.
He inspected the wall.
He returned.
He entered again through the Valley Gate.
passages.original: וָאֶֽעֱבֹר֙ אֶל־ שַׁ֣עַר הָעַ֔יִן וְאֶל־ בְּרֵכַ֖ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵין־ מָק֥וֹם לַבְּהֵמָ֖ה לַעֲבֹ֥ר תַּחְתָּֽי׃ וָאֱהִ֨י עֹלֶ֤ה בַנַּ֙חַל֙ לַ֔יְלָה וָאֱהִ֥י שֹׂבֵ֖ר בַּחוֹמָ֑ה וָאָשׁ֗וּב וָאָב֛וֹא בְּשַׁ֥עַר הַגַּ֖יְא וָאָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for I had not yet told the Jews or priests or nobles or officials or any other workers.
passages.sermon:
I had not told anyone about my actions.
The officials did not know where I had gone.
The officials did not know what I was doing.
I had not told the Jews.
I had not told the priests.
I had not told the nobles.
I had not told the other officials.
I had not told any of the workers.
passages.original: וְהַסְּגָנִ֗ים לֹ֤א יָדְעוּ֙ אָ֣נָה הָלַ֔כְתִּי וּמָ֖ה אֲנִ֣י עֹשֶׂ֑ה וְלַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְלַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים וְלַחֹרִ֣ים וְלַסְּגָנִ֗ים וּלְיֶ֙תֶר֙ עֹשֵׂ֣ה הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה עַד־ כֵּ֖ן לֹ֥א הִגַּֽדְתִּי׃

passages.text: Then I said to them, “You see the trouble we are in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned down. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we will no longer be a disgrace.”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a leader of the Jews in exile.
He spoke to the people in Jerusalem.
He said, “You see the trouble we are in.
Jerusalem is in ruins.
Its gates have been burned with fire.
Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem.
Then we will no longer be a disgrace.”
passages.original: וָאוֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם אַתֶּ֤ם רֹאִים֙ הָרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲנַ֣חְנוּ בָ֔הּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ חֲרֵבָ֔ה וּשְׁעָרֶ֖יהָ נִצְּת֣וּ בָאֵ֑שׁ לְכ֗וּ וְנִבְנֶה֙ אֶת־ חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְלֹא־ נִהְיֶ֥ה ע֖וֹד חֶרְפָּֽה׃

passages.text: I also told them about the gracious hand of my God upon me, and what the king had said to me. “Let us start rebuilding,” they replied, and they set their hands to this good work.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader of the Jews who returned to Jerusalem.
Nehemiah spoke to the people in Jerusalem.
He told them about his God.
He said that God had shown him kindness.
He said that God’s hand was good upon him.
He also told them what the king had said to him.
The people listened to Nehemiah.
They replied, “Let us get up and build.”
They prepared themselves to do this good work.
passages.original: וָאַגִּ֨יד לָהֶ֜ם אֶת־ יַ֣ד אֱלֹהַ֗י אֲשֶׁר־ הִיא֙ טוֹבָ֣ה עָלַ֔י וְאַף־ דִּבְרֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־ לִ֑י וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֔ינוּ וַיְחַזְּק֥וּ יְדֵיהֶ֖ם לַטּוֹבָֽה׃פ

passages.text: But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about this, they mocked us and ridiculed us, saying, “What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?”
passages.sermon:
Sanballat was a Horonite.
Tobiah was an Ammonite official.
Geshem was an Arab.
These three men heard about our plan to rebuild Jerusalem’s wall.
They mocked us.
They ridiculed us.
They said, “What are you doing?”
They asked, “Are you rebelling against the king?”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַע֩ סַנְבַלַּ֨ט הַחֹרֹנִ֜י וְטֹבִיָּ֣ה׀ הָעֶ֣בֶד הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֗י וְגֶ֙שֶׁם֙ הָֽעַרְבִ֔י וַיַּלְעִ֣גוּ לָ֔נוּ וַיִּבְז֖וּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ מָֽה־ הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֔ים הַעַ֥ל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אַתֶּ֥ם מֹרְדִֽים׃

passages.text: So I answered them and said, “The God of heaven is the One who will grant us success. We, His servants, will start rebuilding, but you have no portion, right, or claim in Jerusalem.”
passages.sermon:
I answered them.
I spoke to them directly.
The God of heaven will give us success.
We are His servants.
We will rise up.
We will rebuild.
You have no share in Jerusalem.
You have no right in Jerusalem.
You have no claim or remembrance in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וָאָשִׁ֨יב אוֹתָ֜ם דָּבָ֗ר וָאוֹמַ֤ר לָהֶם֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם ה֚וּא יַצְלִ֣יחַֽ לָ֔נוּ וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֑ינוּ וְלָכֶ֗ם אֵֽין־ חֵ֧לֶק וּצְדָקָ֛ה וְזִכָּר֖וֹן בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
